11
Hardware bugs are expensive
A bug found after fabrication is VERY expensive
e.g. Intel’s Pentium FDIV bug (1994): a ~$475M write-off.
And LLMs are starting to optimise hardware designs too.
e.g. AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind, 2025) proposed a Verilog rewrite of an arithmetic circuit for Google’s TPUs.
So we want specifications.
12
Existing approaches
Templates
a == b a |-> ##1 b a <= b
Limited expressivity, and really, really big sets of assertions (most of which don’t hold)
LLMs
Unreliable, and can’t typically reason well about weird edge cases
Humans
Expensive… and they get sad if you give them too many boring, hard tasks
We’re going to use formal synthesis instead.

15
∃Φ. ∀ inputs .H ⊨ Φ
Example: the max of three inputs
// return the max of three inputs module max3 (   input  [7:0] a, b, c,   output [7:0] result );   wire [7:0] d;   assign d = (a >= b) ? a : b;   assign result = (d >= c) ? d : c; endmodule
Assertions we’d like to find:
assert property (a <= result);
assert property (d <= result);
They relate several signals at once: outside the reach of most template-based miners.
If >= were mistyped as <, both assertions would fail.
16
Synthesis from examples
Encoding H ⊨ α directly means unrolling the transition system. Instead, we use examples:
Positive examples
reachable states, from simulation traces.
Negative example
a random unreachable state, checked by a model checker.
Counterexamples
reachable states the verifier finds that α gets wrong: added to the positives
∃Φ . (∀s ∈ S+ . Φ(s+) = ⊤) ∧ Φ(s-) = ⊥

Temporal properties
Some bugs are about what happens next: broken state machines, non-atomic access checks, …
now (t)
a, b, req, …
k clock cycles
later (t + k)
a′, b′, ack′, …
Copy every variable, then synthesise implications:
Expr ::= Bool(now) ⟹ Bool(later)
assert property (req |-> ##1 ack);
“if req now, then ack one cycle later”
21
Temporal negative examples
A negative example is now a pair of states: (now, later)
→
an unreachable state now, and a state reachable from it later
→
a reachable state now, and a later state that can’t follow it
Both states unreachable? Too imprecise to refine the assertions, so we don’t use those pairs.
Verification
Temporal assertions are checked with bounded model checking (EBMC), so they come with bounded guarantees.
22
Is a specification any good?
A good specification should notice when the design changes.
original H
assign d = (a >= b) ? a : b;
H ⊨ Φ
mutant H′
assign d = (a <  b) ? a : b;
H′ ⊭ Φ detected!
MD-rate = |{ H′ ∈ M : H′ ⊭ Φ }| / |M|

Generating mutants
Where in the Verilog
Rewrite to
Example
Gates: and, or, nand, nor, xor, xnor, not, buf
another gate
and(y, a, b) → nor(y, a, b)
Bitwise operators: &, |, ^
another bitwise op
x & y → x | y
Arithmetic operators: +, −, *, /, %
another arithmetic op
a + b → a * b
Relational operators: ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=
another comparison
a >= b → a < b
Boolean variables
its negation
en → !en
Bit-vector literals
a random value
8'd5 → 8'd173
Each operator: apply one applicable rule, chosen at random
Each boolean variable: negate it
Each literal: replace it with a random value
Each mutant changes the design in exactly one place. It is detected if H ⊨ A but H′ ⊭ A (EBMC, k-induction).

Greedy hitting set: take the variables that appear in the most predicates first.
∀ distributes over ∧, so the unsat core points at the predicates to blame.
In practice the core is usually one predicate: we add one variable at a time.

43
The cache’s environment
The property: non-interference
Two copies of a way-partitioned cache. The attacker gets the same ways and makes the same accesses in both; the victim may do anything.
copy 1 attacker + victim run A
copy 2 attacker + victim run B
Every attacker access hits in copy 1 ⇔ it hits in copy 2, at every step
The environment: assumptions
The cache runs inside a system, so the inputs are constrained
assume (|attacker_hitmap); if (choice == 2'b00) begin   assume (hitmap1 == attacker_hitmap         && hitmap2 == attacker_hitmap);   ... end
System property holds under the assumptions, but not for arbitrary inputs.
To mine the auxiliary invariants, we need to mine under assumptions
Cache designs from Godbole, Ye, Manerkar & Seshia, FMCAD 2023

Example: comparing two arrays
int check(int *a, int *b, int n) {   for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {     if (a[i] != b[i]) {       return 0;     }   }   return 1; }
First verified spec: kills no mutants
ensures \result == 0 || \result == 1;
Surviving mutant, fed back to the LLM:
- if (a[i] != b[i]) { + if (a[i] <  b[i]) {
Refined spec: kills all the mutants
ensures \result == 0 || \result == 1; ensures \result == 1 ==>   (\forall integer k; 0 <= k < n ==> a[k] == b[k]); ensures \result == 0 ==>   (\exists integer k; 0 <= k < n && a[k] != b[k]); loop invariant \forall integer k;   0 <= k < i ==> a[k] == b[k];
51
Verifier-guided proof repair
The LLM may add
  • loop invariants
  • assertions
  • quantifier triggers
  • termination measures
…but must not
  • change the executable Rust
  • weaken the migrated pre/post conditions
  • add assumptions
fn mul(a: i32, b: i32) -> (result: i32)   ...   invariant     // existing invariants unchanged +   a > 0 ==> i32::MIN as int <= (a - x) * b, +   a > 0 ==> (a - x) * b <= i32::MAX as int, +   a > 0 ==> 0 <= x,
Three added loop invariants and Verus proves the translated function, with no changes to code or specs.
